title: NestJS Modular Monolith: Modules, Dependency Injection & Boundaries
concept: Structure a Node.js backend as one deployable with clear modules inside: providers and dependency injection, module imports and exports, provider scopes, DTO validation, thin controllers, domain services and error mapping, and how to break a circular dependency, each taught with the NestJS model and graded with small TypeScript programs.
description: An intermediate course for backend developers whose service has grown into a tangle of files that all import each other. Every lesson starts from a problem on the CodeDev learning platform - a CourseModule and an EnrollmentModule that call each other until the app will not boot, a controller that holds every business rule, a progress bar that jumps backwards when a request is retried, a DTO generated by an AI assistant that lets unknown fields reach the database - and fixes it with the ideas NestJS is built on: modules that own their providers and export a small public surface, constructor injection and a container that wires it, provider scopes, validation at the edge, services that hold the domain rules, domain errors mapped to HTTP in one place, and a dependency direction you can check. The code runner has no npm packages, so you build each mechanism in plain TypeScript - a tiny DI container, a module boundary checker, an enrollment and a progress service - and the same reasoning carries straight into a real NestJS app. 10 lessons with quizzes on real code and hands-on TypeScript challenges.
